rationale: The diagnosis (FMB slope of 4.06 with zero FF5 alpha implies a cross-industry capital-intensity tilt) is sound and worth resolving, but swapping RANK for IND_RANK in an otherwise identical expression is the textbook cosmetic variant the objective warns against rather than a substantively different construction.

The level-to-change reframing is a genuinely distinct state-change mechanism, but the construction is partly self-referential — a jump in EBITDA mechanically shrinks capx/MAX(ebitda,dp), so the "reinvestment drop" leg will partially reproduce profitability momentum already captured by the first leg, and a level-vs-change horse race would be needed to interpret any result.

Net-to-gross PP&E as a cumulative-non-replacement stock is a real cross-theme quantity that is neither a one-year flow nor an FF5 loading, and the stated conditioning logic (old capital means harvesting only when profitable, obsolescence otherwise) is internally consistent with the multiplicative form; the main risk is that the ratio is dominated by depreciation-schedule and industry heterogeneity rather than managerial restraint.

The investment leg is close to Titman-Wei-Xie abnormal capital investment (capex benchmarked to the firm's own recent history), so novelty rests entirely on the profitability gate, and a 5-observation TS_RANK yields only five distinct values, which will blunt cross-sectional resolution.

Margin level interacted with change in asset turnover is the DuPont decomposition studied by Soliman (2008), whose central published result is precisely that ΔATO positively predicts returns, so this is a direct rediscovery dressed in new language.

This mechanically averages two investment legs already tested in the archive under the same margin gate, so it will almost certainly deliver an alpha between the two parents and cannot cleanly answer the stated independence question — a correlation check or a residualized second leg would be far more informative than a blended composite.
